column2: twenty-five years before this site existed, DERRICK WAS SEARCHING FOR HIS FATHER'S SURNAME IN GERMANY on a dial-up genealogy portal, and kept the printout. It travelled with his mother's birth and death papers to Portugal in 2010. THE QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE IS ANSWERING IS ONE HE ASKED FIRST.

Database: Germany Telephone and Address Listings. COMBINED MATCHES: 16. The surviving page shows the first six; TEN MORE WERE NOT PHOTOGRAPHED and are worth having if the rest of the printout survives.

GERMAN NUMBERS ARE REASSIGNED, and a twenty-five-year-old subscriber line now reaches a stranger; the genealogical value is in the DIALLING CODE, which locates the household, and that is published. This archive publishes full numbers from the Berlin books of the 1970s because a constant number across volumes is what proves one household — there is only one volume here, so the number proves nothing and could annoy somebody.

column1: *** THREE OF THE SIX ARE IN DUISBURG, ALL ON THE 0203 CODE ***
column2: Kurt, Rainer and Z., and two of the three numbers sit in the same exchange range. A RARE SURNAME CLUSTERING IN ONE RUHR CITY is the shape of a family that moved together, and Duisburg is a steel town that took large numbers of East Prussian and Silesian expellees after 1945. Bochum, forty kilometres away, makes it four of six in the Ruhr.

column1: and one of them is called KURT
column2: a namesake of this archive's central figure, KURT ISRAEL LUWINSKI, born Berlin 1912 and died Johannesburg 1968. A DIFFERENT MAN ENTIRELY and no connection is claimed; recorded because the coincidence will occur to the next reader as it occurred to this one.

column1: the Berlin one is the interesting one
column2: CHRISTA, at AFRIKANISCHE STRASSE 32, D-13351 BERLIN.

column1: *** AND THE 1938 ADRESSBUCH HAS A LEIBHOLZ AT AFRIKANISCHE STRASSE 37 ***
column2: C, Kaufm., N65 Afrikanische Str 37 stands in the 1938 Berliner Adressbuch's run of ten Leibholz householders. N65 AND D-13351 ARE BOTH WEDDING. The same street, five doors apart, sixty-three years apart, one from each of the two surnames this archive follows.

column1: how much weight that carries, which is very little
column2: AFRIKANISCHE STRASSE IS LONG, both surnames existed in Berlin independently of this family, and nothing whatever connects a 2001 telephone subscriber to a 1938 householder. IT IS WRITTEN DOWN SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT HAVE TO NOTICE IT TWICE, and so that noticing it is not mistaken for finding something.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IS WORTH DOING WITH IT ----------------

column2: if the remaining pages survive in the family's papers they would complete the 2001 distribution. THE GERMAN SPREAD OF A RARE SURNAME IS EVIDENCE ABOUT WHERE A FAMILY CAME FROM, and this archive has spent weeks on the Berlin directories without ever looking at the post-war Federal Republic outside Berlin.

none of these people is joined to Kurt Luwinski of Prenzlauer Berg by any document. THEY SHARE A SURNAME AND A COUNTRY. The archive's register keeps such people separate from the family proper for exactly this reason.
